# Zoning Analysis: 1256 N Artesian Ave, Chicago, IL
**PIN:** 16012280240000 | **West Town (Community Area 24)**

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3 (Residential Single-Family, Subsection 3)**, per the City of Chicago's official GIS zoning system. You can verify this on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

## 2. Is a 3+ Unit Residential Building Permitted By Right?

**No.** RS-3 is a low-density single-family residential district. The "RS" designation is designed for detached single-family and, under limited circumstances, two-unit buildings. A building with 3 or more dwelling units is **not permitted by right** in RS-3.

To achieve 3+ units, you would need to pursue a **rezoning** to a higher-density residential classification (e.g., RT-4, RM-4, or higher), which requires City Council approval through the zoning amendment process.

> **Note on your lot size:** At approximately 3,150 sq ft, the lot is quite small — density constraints would bind tightly even at a higher zoning classification (see §4 below). [1][2]

---

## 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards in RS-3

The following apply under RS-3 per [2]:

- **Minimum Lot Area per Dwelling Unit (MLA/DU):**
  - **RS-3 standard:** 2,500 sq ft per dwelling unit
  - **RS-3 exception** [2]: The MLA/DU may be reduced to **1,500 sq ft per unit** when 60% or more of the zoning lots on the same side of the street between the two nearest intersecting streets are lawfully improved with buildings containing more than one dwelling unit, **or** when the property falls within "Predominance of the Block" boundaries defined by [1]. This exception **only allows establishment of a two-unit building** — it does not permit more than two units in RS-3 under any circumstance.

- **FAR (Floor-Area Ratio):** Specific FAR limits for RS-3 are not included in the retrieved code sections. You should verify the applicable FAR in **§ 17-2-0300** of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance directly (available at [Chicago Municipal Code Online](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago_zoningordinance.html)).

- **Off-Street Parking — Location Standards** [3]:
  - Parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line (except when accessed by a permitted driveway from the front property line).
  - Required parking for residential uses must be on the same zoning lot as the units served.

- **Height Limits and Front/Side/Rear Setbacks:** The specific numeric values for RS-3 height limits and setback requirements are **not contained in the retrieved code sections**. These are found in **§ 17-2-0400** (setbacks) and **§ 17-2-0500** (height) of the Zoning Ordinance — verify directly in the municipal code or with the Chicago Department of Planning and Development (DPD).

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

Several overlays apply to this parcel:

- **ADU-Eligible Area** [1][5]: This parcel falls within a designated **Additional Dwelling Unit (ADU) Allowed RS Area** under [1]. This means that — on a single-family or two-flat lot — you may be able to add a **conversion unit** (internal ADU) or a **coach house** (accessory dwelling unit in the rear) as additional units beyond the base RS-3 allowance. Coach houses in RS-3 must comply with [5], including:
  - Maximum height of **22 feet**
  - At least **3 feet of unobstructed open space** from at least one side property line for the full wall length
  - Coach house parking may be reduced or waived via administrative adjustment per [5]
  - A building permit for a new coach house may not be issued unless the lot complies with [1]
  - Enforcement is by the **Department of Housing** at ADU pre-certification [1]

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone**: This parcel is located within an ARO zone. The West Town community area has **20 ARO-related affordable housing projects totaling 291 units** on record. If you pursue a rezoning and develop market-rate units above a threshold number, ARO affordability requirements may be triggered. Verify the applicable threshold and contribution options with the Department of Housing.

- **Special District**: The parcel is within a designated Special District overlay. The specific name and restrictions of this special district were not available in the retrieved data — you should verify with DPD what this designation entails for this block.

- **No Planned Development**: This parcel is **not** within a Planned Development.
- **No Landmark or Historic District**: Not a landmark building; not in a local landmark district or National Register historic district.
- **Not on a Pedestrian Street**: No pedestrian street overlay applies.
- **No Special Service Area (SSA)**: This parcel is not within an SSA.
- **Not TOD-Eligible**: This parcel does **not** qualify for Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) density or parking bonuses under the Connected Communities Ordinance (see §5 below for transit context).

**Flood Zone:** FEMA Zone **X** (Area of Minimal Flood Hazard) — this parcel is **not** in a Special Flood Hazard Area. No flood insurance is required. No brownfield sites are nearby.

---

## 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reductions

Under [3], RS-3 requires off-street parking spaces to be located on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served. Specific **numeric parking ratios** (e.g., spaces per unit) for RS-3 are in **§ 17-10-0100** of the Zoning Ordinance — the retrieved sections did not include those figures.

**Transit Context (Not TOD-Eligible):**
The nearest CTA rail is the **Damen Blue Line station** (approximately 0.68 miles away), and the nearest Metra is **Western Ave / Milwaukee North** (approximately 1.04 miles away). However, as noted above, this parcel is **not designated as TOD-eligible**, so no automatic parking reductions or density bonuses under the Connected Communities Ordinance apply.

For coach houses specifically, [5] notes that parking required for the principal building may be reduced or waived via administrative adjustment, and coach houses themselves may be established without any accessory parking requirement.

---

## 6. Maximum Units By Right — Could You Build 6 Units?

**By right in RS-3: Maximum 1 unit (detached house); up to 2 units under the MLA/DU exception only if block conditions are met.**

Here is the math on your ~3,150 sq ft lot:

| Scenario | MLA/DU Required | Units Supported by Lot Size |
|---|---|---|
| RS-3 standard | 2,500 sq ft/unit | **1 unit** |
| RS-3 exception (if block qualifies) [2] | 1,500 sq ft/unit | **2 units** (the exception caps at 2 regardless) |
| + Coach house (ADU area) [1][5] | Subject to ADU rules | Potentially **+1 ADU/coach house** on top of principal building |

**Maximum achievable by right: approximately 2–3 units** (2-flat principal building + 1 ADU/coach house), and only if:
- The block's predominance condition is satisfied [2], AND
- ADU pre-certification requirements are met [1]

**Can you build 6 units?**
**No — not by right.** To build 6 units you would need to rezone to at minimum **RM-4** or higher. Even then, on a 3,150 sq ft lot, the MLA/DU standard at RM-4 is approximately 1,000 sq ft/unit (verify in § 17-2-0303), which would theoretically support about 3 units — still well short of
